Description: Presenter shares their screen within the first 2 minutes of the meeting.
No significant audio or video issues that impaired the demo experience (echo, lag, muting problems).
Presenter briefly previews what the demo will cover before diving in.
Presenter acknowledges attendees by name and confirms who is on the call.
Presenter names the product/platform being demonstrated.
The main product offering is explained in a way a first-time viewer would understand.
At least the core features of the product are shown with live examples.
The demo follows a logical flow rather than jumping between unrelated sections.
Presenter uses real or realistic data/examples rather than placeholder/dummy content.
Demo moves at a pace the audience can follow — not too fast or too slow.
Presenter pauses to ask if attendees have questions, rather than only at the end.
When attendees ask questions they are answered directly and not deflected.
Presenter invites attendees to participate (e.g., 'what would you like to see next?').
No long monologues without checking in with attendees.
Presenter shows genuine enthusiasm about the product rather than a flat monotone delivery.
No incorrect claims about what the product can or cannot do.
Demo runs without crashes, errors, or broken features that undermine credibility.
Numbers and data shown on screen are realistic and accurate.
When asked about missing features, presenter is honest rather than making false promises.
If pricing comes up, it is addressed clearly or deferred to a documented next step.
If attendees compare to competitors, presenter responds confidently without disparagement.
Presenter acknowledges concerns rather than talking over them.
Presenter does not use guilt or false urgency to push for a decision.
Presenter briefly recaps what was shown and key takeaways.
A concrete next step is proposed (trial signup, follow-up call, send materials).
A specific date/time for follow-up is agreed rather than leaving it open-ended.
Demo ends with a courteous thank-you and goodbye.
Presenter offers to share the recording or supplementary materials.
No unprofessional language or inappropriate remarks.
Presenter paraphrases or references what attendees said.
If an attendee repeats a question, presenter re-explains patiently.
Presenter speaks clearly without excessive filler words or uncertainty on core facts.
Presenter navigates between screens and tabs smoothly without confusion.
